data: Smarter search, safer imports, smoother audio
Semantic search gains proper filter support, the importer hardens against edge cases, and audio waveforms move to crisp SVGs.

AssetHoard v0.1.11 release notes

Smarter search, safer imports, smoother audio

This release sharpens semantic search with real filter support, makes the importer safer when several imports are running at once, and introduces crisper waverforms. There is also a solid performance pass across bundle loading asset reloads.

🔍 Search and discovery

We've promoted Search from experiments to a standard feature, and are continuing to add improvements along the way.

  • Semantic search filters: filters now apply to semantic queries, so you can combine natural-language search with the same filters you already use for keyword search
  • Search settings section: a new Search area in Settings makes semantic search easy to configure and manage
  • Case-insensitive tags: tags now match regardless of case, and a one-off migration merges any existing duplicates so your library stays tidy
  • Sort by duration: sort audio and video assets by length, with cleaner duration and file-size formatting in the grid
  • Stable sort order: columns that cannot be sorted directly now fall back to sorting by name, keeping the order predictable

📥 Import pipeline

A series of improvements and bug fixes have made for the import system. Still lots more to do!

  • Concurrent import tracking: each import is assigned its own ID, so notifications stay accurate when several imports are running side by side
  • 🐛 Packages now import into the correct folder: unitypackages were being improted without a bundle (even when they were supposed to be) - this has been fixed
  • 🐛 Package bundle polish: the "Create sub-bundle" option is now hidden on package bundles where it does not apply
  • Improved Cover Image Setting speeds up processing over setting cover images at time of import
  • Improved thumbnail generation around 300% increase in speed, and added more stability
  • Leaner memory footprint: reduced the memory footprint requirements of semantic search indexing

🔊 Audio

Improved the display and future capability of the waveforms. For now, it's improved visuals, but it unlocks drag and export, theme support, and more.

  • Waveforms: waveform thumbnails are now rendering dynmically instead of thumbnailed, resulting in crisper rendering
  • Minimum duration display: very short audio assets now show their actual length instead of rendering as 0:00

⚡ Performance

  • Batched bundle loading: bundles and their assets load in batches, cutting database round-trips (~15% increase in speed)
  • Atomic asset reload: bulk operations now reload via a merge, so there is no flash of stale data afterwards
  • Faster image thumbnails: a quicker downscaling algorithm speeds up thumbnail generation (benchmarked at ~300% increase in speed)
  • Smoother drag hovers: hover updates during drag operations are smoother and less cpu intensive (slight improvement in speed and responsiveness)

✨ Bundles and UI polish

  • Inline bundle rename: rename bundles directly in the sidebar
  • Selection hygiene: navigating into a bundle now clears any stale main-grid selection, so bulk actions always target what you expect
  • DB Maintenance: soft-deleted records are cleaned up in the background once a day, and a toast reports how much space has been reclaimed
  • DB corrupted screen: If the AssetHoard DB is corrupted (power outage, etc.) then a popup is displayed on boot giving the user the option to restore from an automatic backup

🐧 Platform

  • Wayland rendering fix: Wayland with Nvidia could stop the Assethoard from running, a small fix to attempt to work around this

🛠 Under the hood

Since we're all devs, some behind the scenes stuff.

  • A broad dependency refresh across all the dependencies used by AssetHoard are now 100% up to date

May your waveforms be crisp and your imports be orderly.

Happy hoarding.
Themes, import resume, and macOS signing
Customise your workspace with new themes, pick up interrupted imports where you left off, and macOS code signing and notarisation.

AssetHoard v0.1.10 release notes

Themes, import resume, and macOS signing

AssetHoard now ships with a theme system and the ability to resume imports that were interrupted mid-flight. macOS builds are properly code-signed and notarised, and there is a solid round of settings polish and search improvements.

🔑 Preparing for Open Beta - Licensing

As AssetHoard is maturing we are starting to get the app ready for Open Beta. There's a transitional period before we start to require a license to continue using AssetHoard.

The license is a one-time purchase, which provides upgrades for life. While in Open Beta we'll have a small dismissable reminder that this is coming.

🎨 Theme Support

Nine built-in themes ship with this release. Pick one from Settings and your choice is saved automatically.

  • themes included — Classic, Midnight, Ember, Slate, Catppuccin, Nord, Rosé Pine, Tokyo Night, Catppuccin Latte

UI Improvements

  • Details panel toggle — show or hide the details panel with a keyboard shortcut; your preference is saved automatically
  • Sidebar tooltips — hover over sidebar items for quick context
  • Right-aligned project counts — project counts now sit neatly on the right side of the sidebar
  • Copy file path — a new button in asset details copies the full file path to your clipboard

📥 Importer Improvements

  • Auto-resume on restart — if the app exits during an import, you can choose to pick up where it left off next time you launch (see notifications in the app)
  • Faster material thumbnails — large speed improvements for Material thumbnails
  • AVIF support — AssetHoard now recognises and previews .avif images

🔍 Search and filtering

  • Extension filter — search for *.png or any glob pattern to filter assets by file extension
  • Improved pagination — search results now paginate more reliably with better near-bottom scroll detection

🍎 macOS code signing

  • Signed and notarised builds — macOS releases are now properly code-signed with entitlements and notarised via the Apple notary service

🛠 More improvements

  • UNC and network path support — drag-and-drop now works with Windows SMB and NAS paths
  • Keyboard shortcut for settings — jump straight into settings without touching the mouse

May your assets be organised and your themes be aesthetic.

Happy hoarding.
Sharp pixel rendering, and a new Workbench

A new Pixel Renderer keeps sprites crisp on import across PNG, GIF, TGA, Photoshop, Krita, and more. Alongside it, the Workbench arrives as a scratchpad for gathering assets before dropping them into a project.

AssetHoard v0.1.12 release notes

Sharp pixel rendering, and a new Workbench

The headline feature in this release is the Pixel Renderer, a refactor in how assets are displayed that keeps pixel art crisp without any manual setup. Alongside that, the new Workbench gives you a scratchpad for gathering assets before dropping them into a project, and everyday tasks feel smoother with better undo, cleaner previews, and friendlier bundles.

🎨 Pixel art done right

AssetHoard now recognises pixel art on import automatically and keeps those tiny sprites crisp instead of blurry. It works across PNG, GIF, TGA, Photoshop, Krita, and more.

  • Automatic detection: pixel art is picked up on import without any manual tagging
  • Sharp rendering: sprites display with nearest-neighbour scaling, so pixels stay pixels
  • Category defaults: mark an entire category as pixel art and every asset inside inherits the setting
  • Per-asset override: override the default on individual assets when you need to

The real magic here is a large refactor of how we show assets. We've introduced a new concept called renderers. First cab off the rank is the Pixel Renderer, but we'll be extending to other renderers in the future for 3D, Materials, and packages like Godot.

🧰 A New Workbench

A dedicated place to collect assets before committing them to a project. Pick things up as you browse, review what you have, and send the whole lot to a project in a single click. There's an option in settings -> ui to turn this off if you won't need it.

  • Dedicated area: the Workbench has its own sidebar panel and full-page view
  • Drag in from the library: drop any assets or bundles onto the Workbench as you browse

  • Bulk-add to a project: send everything you have collected to a project in a single click
  • Library badges: items sitting on the Workbench get a small badge in the library, so you always know what has already been picked up
  • Status bar counter: a running count shows how many items you are carrying at any time
  • Full undo and redo: adding and removing from the Workbench is fully reversible
  • Recent projects: the Workbench remembers your most recent projects, so it is quick to get back to where you were

📦 Bundles got friendlier

  • Bundle descriptions: add notes on each bundle to capture what it is for
  • Shift-click expand: Shift and click the expand arrow in the sidebar to open or close a whole nested tree at once
  • Cleaner move undo: undoing a bundle move now reverses the whole thing in one step, instead of two
  • Search results polish: bundle cover images and icons now appear correctly in search results
  • Sensible move rules: bundles now visually show they can't be dropped in themselves
  • 🐛 Bundles stay populated: re-opening a recently viewed bundle now reliably shows its assets, even after a library refresh has cleared the in-memory asset cache. No more F5.

🖼 Previews and layout

  • Wider preview panel: the asset preview can now be stretched up to 1000px
  • 3D & Sprite play buttons: are now below the drag handle
  • Easier resize handle: the handle is easier to find and grab
  • Wrapping file paths: long file paths now wrap instead of running off the screen
  • 🐛 Tidier list view: columns line up properly, and bundles now show their category

✨ Quality of life

  • Install Now on Mac: the "Install Now" action in the updater now works correctly, and keeps any in-progress imports safe across the restart
  • 🐛 Blender previews on Linux: a fix for Blender thumbnail previews on Linux
  • Polish throughout: various small fixes and visual tidies across the app

May your Workbench be full and your pixels be sharp.

Happy hoarding.
